seo.title: About Verde Law — Humanitarian Immigration Firm
seo.description: A Miami-based firm founded to make quality immigration representation accessible. 600+ families. 50 states. One mission.

about.title: A firm built for the people the system is hardest on.
about.subtitle: Verde Law was founded with a single idea: that every immigrant in the United States deserves an attorney who answers the phone, speaks their language, and fights like it's personal.

story.title: From law school bet to 600 families strong.
story.p1: Rafael Verde founded Verde Law in 2024, straight out of Georgetown Law — before most of his classmates had decided which firm to join. The bet was simple: that there was a real market for a humanitarian immigration firm that treated Spanish-speaking families the way corporate clients get treated — with urgency, with respect, and with an attorney who actually knows their name.
story.p2: The first year was two attorneys and a single office in Coral Way. Today the team is 22 people strong, serving clients in all fifty states, from bond hearings at Krome to federal appeals in the Eleventh Circuit.
story.p3: Our TikTok audience is over 61,000 and growing, because free education matters as much as paid representation.
story.p4: Every new case still gets Rafael's personal review. That hasn't changed. It won't change.

mission.title: Why we do this.
mission.quote: We believe every immigrant deserves quality legal representation — regardless of their financial situation.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.desc: Flat fees. Payment plans. Free consultations. Language access in four languages. Representation should never depend on who you know or what you can pay up front.

excellence.title: Excellence
excellence.desc: We prepare every case like it's heading to federal court. Evidence binders, expert declarations, mock hearings, expert coordination. The standard doesn't drop when the client can't afford a retainer.

humanity.title: Humanity
humanity.desc: The people on the other side of our desk are scared, exhausted, and out of options. We meet them with patience and respect, every time. That's not a nice-to-have — it's the job.
